QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_66

question.text: What reporting obligations do large position holders have in the ETIRD market?

answer.text: Large position holders must report their positions to the exchange, which may share this information with SEBI
There are no reporting obligations for any market participants
Only banks must report; other participants are exempt
Reporting is required only at the end of each financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: In the Exchange Traded Interest Rate Derivatives (ETIRD) segment, exchanges run online surveillance over positions, prices, volumes, open interest and client-level details. Participants holding positions above prescribed category-wise position limits are monitored at member/client level, and the exchange may call for information and share aggregated/large-position data with SEBI for systemic-risk and surveillance purposes. The Trap: Saying there are no reporting obligations contradicts the existence of position limits and exchange surveillance; limiting reporting to banks ignores the category-wise framework that covers all participants; and confining reporting to year-end ignores the ongoing/real-time nature of derivatives surveillance. Note: The specific obligation of "large position holders must report positions to the exchange" is not stated verbatim in the cited NISM-Series-IV pages, which support online surveillance, category-wise position limits and margin short-collection reporting. The framing above reflects general exchange/SEBI surveillance practice for derivative markets rather than a direct workbook citation.
